intro: The Silver-Root Gate reopens beneath the Sídhe Mound. The roots of the world-tree are exposed — each one a living record of every geas ever sworn. The Hollow has begun to rot the roots from the inside.

The rot is spreading through the root system. Each rotten root releases a corrupted geas — a binding promise that serves the Hollow instead of the forest. The bindings are invisible until they tighten.

The root network is fragmenting. Sections of the mound are collapsing into void-space where roots have dissolved. You must cross through living root and dead root simultaneously — one binds, the other dissolves.
The Sídhe Mound's core root — the first geas ever sworn to the forest. The Hollow has wrapped itself around it. The binding is so deep that removing the Hollow may kill the root.
enemy: Root-rot wraiths born from dissolved geas bindings. They do not attack — they bind. Each one wraps around a limb and tightens until the limb belongs to the Hollow.
The wraiths are spreading corrupted geas through the root network. Each corrupted binding makes the next root easier to rot. The infection accelerates.
Hollow geas-thorns — barbed growths that embed corrupted promises into flesh. Each thorn is a geas that serves the Hollow, and removing it breaks the skin it pierced.

The core root guardian — a Hollow entwined with the first geas. It speaks the first promise, but the words are inverted. 'I bind the forest to the void' — the inversion of 'I bind the void to the forest.'
mid: The root-rot wraiths bind, not bite. Do not let them wrap. Each binding is a corrupted geas — and geas cannot be broken without consequence.
The corrupted geas is spreading through the root network. Cut the infected roots — even though cutting roots wounds the forest. Some wounds are necessary.
The geas-thorns embed corrupted promises. Remove them carefully — the promise is corrupted, but the skin it pierced is yours.
The guardian speaks the inverted geas. Do not argue with the inversion — plant a new root. The original geas is still alive beneath the Hollow. Water it with your own conviction.
victory: The first root holds. The rot is slowed — but the root system is vast. The Hollow has learned which roots you protect and which you sacrifice.
The corrupted geas bindings are cut — but the root network is wounded. The forest remembers every cut. The deeper chambers will be harder to heal.
The geas-thorns are removed — but the wounds remain. Each wound is a place where a corrupted promise was torn from flesh. The scars will ache in the deeper chambers.
The core root is reclaimed. The first geas is restored — but the Hollow left a mark. The root now carries both the original promise and the scar of its inversion.
defeat: The root-rot wraiths bound you before you could cut free. Each binding was a corrupted geas. Return when you can distinguish binding from binding.
The corrupted geas spread faster than you could cut. The root network was lost. Return when cutting wounds is better than letting rot spread.
The geas-thorns embedded too deeply. Removing them killed the flesh. Return when the wound of removal is survivable.
The guardian's inverted geas held. You could not plant a new root while the old one was inverted. Return when conviction can water what the Hollow has dried.
codex: The Silver-Root Gate tests whether the deity can heal a living system from the inside. The roots are alive — they feel every cut. The Hollow rots them precisely because the healing requires wounding what you love.
The root-rot wraiths bind rather than bite. A corrupted geas is worse than a wound — because a wound heals, but a binding changes what you are. The deity must cut bindings without cutting the root.

The geas-thorns embed corrupted promises into flesh. Removing them is necessary — but the removal wounds. The Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: some healings require harm. The healer must carry the wound they inflict.

The first geas — 'I bind the void to the forest' — is the foundation of the Tuatha Gate. The Hollow inverted it to 'I bind the forest to the void.' The restoration requires planting a new root that carries the original promise.

intro: The Wild Hunt Echo. The ancient hunt — once the Tuatha's most sacred practice — has been corrupted. The Hollow released the hunt's prey: a void-stag that the hunters cannot catch. The hunt has been running since before the Collapse.
The void-stag is leading the hunt into the root network. Each step of the hunt tramples living roots. The hunters cannot stop — the geas of the hunt drives them. The Hollow uses the geas as a weapon.

The hunt has split. Some hunters follow the void-stag. Some have turned on each other. The geas drives them to hunt — but without prey, they hunt each other. The root network is being trampled by the hunters' own frenzy.

The hunt's origin point. The first stag was caught here — and its antlers were planted as the first root. The Hollow has replaced the antlers with void-antlers. The root growing from them is rotten from the source.
enemy: Corrupted Wild Hunters driven by an unbreakable geas to hunt. They cannot stop. They cannot rest. They hunt because the geas demands it — and the geas is corrupted.
The hunters have turned on each other. The geas does not specify the prey — only the hunting. Without the void-stag to chase, they chase each other. Each fallen hunter feeds the root-rot.
Hollow hunt-hounds — void-entities shaped like the Tuatha's sacred hounds. They track by conviction-scent. The more conviction the deity shows, the more hounds arrive.
The void-stag's guardian — a Hollow wearing the antlers of the first stag. It does not run. It stands at the root's origin and lets the hunt trample everything around it. The trampling is the point.
mid: The hunters are driven by corrupted geas. Do not try to stop them — the geas is unbreakable. Redirect the hunt. Give them a prey worth hunting.
The hunters have turned on each other. The geas does not care what is hunted — only that hunting happens. Redirect the geas toward the Hollow. Let the hunt serve the forest again.
The hunt-hounds track by conviction-scent. Do not hide your conviction — use it. Lead the hounds to the Hollow. Let them hunt what should be hunted.
The void-stag's guardian lets the trampling happen. The trampling is the weapon. Do not stop the trampling — redirect it. Let the hunters trample the Hollow instead of the roots.
victory: The hunt is redirected. The hunters chase the Hollow instead of each other — but the geas is still corrupted. The drive remains. The deeper chambers will test whether the redirection holds.
The hunters are calmed — but only temporarily. The geas drives them still. The root network breathes — but the trampling has left deep wounds.
The hunt-hounds are turned. They track the Hollow's scent now — but the Hollow has no conviction. The hounds will lose the scent in the deeper chambers.
The void-stag's guardian is broken. The void-antlers are removed. But the root growing from the original antlers is scarred. The first hunt is remembered — but the memory carries the Hollow's mark.
defeat: The hunters' geas was unbreakable and you tried to break it. Return when redirection is more powerful than suppression.
The hunters turned on each other faster than you could redirect. The root network was trampled beyond healing. Return when the hunt can serve the forest.
The hunt-hounds tracked your conviction and overwhelmed you. Return when conviction attracts the right hunters — not the wrong hounds.
The guardian let the trampling destroy the root network. You tried to stop the trampling instead of redirecting it. Return when redirection is the only stop that works.
codex: The Wild Hunt Echo tests whether the deity can redirect sacred practices that have been corrupted. The hunt is sacred. The geas is unbreakable. The Hollow weaponizes both — because a sacred practice corrupted is worse than a profane one.

The corrupted geas does not specify the prey — only the hunting. Without prey, the hunters hunt each other. The Hollow's strategy: corrupt the geas, remove the prey, let the sacred practice destroy itself.
The hunt-hounds track by conviction-scent. The more conviction the deity shows, the more hounds arrive. The Hollow uses the deity's own conviction as a beacon — drawing weapons to the wielder.

The void-stag's guardian lets the trampling happen because the trampling is the weapon. The hunt is not the problem — the prey is. By replacing the sacred stag with a void-stag, the Hollow turned the hunt into a tool of destruction without changing the hunt at all.

intro: The Sídhe Court of Broken Bargains. The Hollow has breached the fairy court where the Tuatha make their oldest bargains. Each broken bargain releases a geas-curse — a binding that punishes the breaker. The court is full of curses.

The curses are interacting. Broken bargains are merging into compound geas-curses — bindings that cannot be fulfilled because they contradict each other. The court is a prison of impossible obligations.
The compound curses have spread to the root network. Each root now carries a contradictory binding. The roots cannot grow because they are bound to grow in opposite directions simultaneously.

The court's origin. The first bargain ever made between the Tuatha and the forest — a pact of mutual feeding. The Hollow has broken the bargain and planted a counter-bargain: the forest feeds the void.
enemy: Geas-curse wraiths born from broken bargains. Each one is an unfulfilled obligation that has become hostile. They do not attack — they bind. Each binding is a debt that cannot be paid.
The compound curses create impossible obligations. The deity is bound to do and not-do simultaneously. The binding is real. The fulfillment is impossible. The contradiction is the weapon.
Hollow bargain-breakers. They offer new bargains that seem to resolve the compound curses — but each new bargain creates two new contradictions. The resolution is the trap.
The first bargain's breaker — a Hollow wearing the face of the first Tuatha who made the pact with the forest. It speaks the original bargain in the original voice — but every term is inverted.
mid: The geas-curse wraiths bind with impossible obligations. Do not try to fulfill them — they are designed to be unfulfillable. Break the binding, not the obligation.
The compound curses create contradictions. You are bound to do and not-do. The way out is a third option — neither doing nor not-doing, but transforming the obligation itself.
The bargain-breakers offer resolutions that create more contradictions. Do not accept new bargains. Restore the original — the first pact was fair before the inversion.
The first bargain's breaker speaks the inverted terms. Do not argue with the inversion. Plant the original terms as a new root. Let the original grow over the inversion.
victory: The court is stabilized — but the curses linger. The impossible obligations cannot be fulfilled, but the bindings can be loosened. The deeper chambers will test whether the loosening holds.
The compound curses are separated — but each individual curse still binds. The root network can grow again — but slowly, and in pain.
The bargain-breakers are silenced — but their offers echo. The temptation of resolution-through-new-bargains remains. The deeper chambers will offer easier bargains.
The first bargain is restored. The original pact — mutual feeding between Tuatha and forest — is renewed. But the scar of the inversion remains. The forest remembers being fed to the void.
defeat: The geas-curse wraiths bound you with impossible obligations. You tried to fulfill them. Return when breaking the binding is better than fulfilling the unfulfillable.
The compound curses created contradictions you could not resolve. You tried to do and not-do. Return when the third option — transformation — is visible.
The bargain-breakers' resolutions created more contradictions. You accepted the new bargains. Return when the original is more valuable than the resolution.
The first bargain's inversion held. You argued with the inverted terms. Return when planting the original is more powerful than arguing with the inversion.
codex: The Sídhe Court tests whether the deity can navigate impossible obligations. Broken bargains create geas-curses — bindings that punish the breaker. The Hollow breaks bargains deliberately to weaponize the curses.

The compound curses are the Hollow's most elegant Tuatha weapon: two bindings that contradict each other. Fulfilling one breaks the other, which creates a new curse. The deity must find a third option — transforming the obligation rather than fulfilling or breaking it.

The bargain-breakers offer resolutions that create more contradictions. The Hollow's strategy: every resolution is a new bargain, and every new bargain is a new vulnerability. The defense is to restore the original — the first pact was fair before the corruption.

The first bargain — mutual feeding between Tuatha and forest — is the Tuatha Gate's foundation. The Hollow inverted it to 'the forest feeds the void.' The restoration requires replanting the original terms — but the forest remembers being eaten. Trust is not easily regrown.

intro: The Root Storm. The root network has been so compromised by rot, curses, and corrupted geas that it has begun to fight itself. The roots are growing against each other — each one trying to fulfill a different corrupted binding.

The root-storm is intensifying. Roots are tearing through the Sídhe Mound, destroying each other. The violence is the Hollow's design — each root that dies feeds the void. The root network is consuming itself.
The storm has reached the trial road. Roots burst through the ground without warning, binding and crushing. The deity must walk a road that is being destroyed by the very system meant to support it.

The storm's eye. The original root — the first geas — is the only root not fighting. It stands at the center of the storm, untouched. But it is shrinking. Every root that dies takes a piece of the original with it.
enemy: Storm-driven roots attacking anything that moves. Each root is fulfilling a corrupted geas — binding, crushing, or dissolving. They do not distinguish friend from foe. They only fulfill.
The roots are combining attacks. Multiple corrupted geas create compound root-attacks — bindings that crush while dissolving. The duality is the weapon.
Hollow root-singers. They sing corrupted geas to the roots, driving the storm. Each song is a binding that makes roots fight. The singers are the storm's engine.
The storm's eye guardian — a Hollow standing beside the original root, singing the one song that would calm the storm. But the song is inverted: it would calm the roots by killing them all at once.
mid: The storm-driven roots attack without discrimination. Do not fight the roots — fight the singers. The roots are victims of the corrupted geas, not enemies.
The compound root-attacks bind and dissolve simultaneously. You cannot escape both — but you can cut the geas that drives them. Cut the song, not the root.
The root-singers drive the storm with corrupted geas. Silence the singers — but carefully. Killing a singer releases its geas into the nearest root, making it stronger.
The guardian sings the inverted calming song. Do not let it finish — the song would calm the roots by killing them. Sing the original: the song that calms by healing, not by ending.
victory: The storm is calmed — but the root network is devastated. Half the roots are dead. The surviving roots carry the scars. The forest will regrow — but slowly, and with memory.
The compound root-attacks are stopped — but the corrupted geas lingers in the surviving roots. Each root could reignite at any time. The deeper chambers will test whether the calm holds.
The root-singers are silenced — but their songs echo in the root network. The echoes could reawaken the storm. The deeper chambers will be louder with corrupted geas.
The storm's eye is reclaimed. The original root is alive — diminished, but alive. The calming song is restored. But the root network is half-dead, and the dead roots feed the void.
defeat: The storm-driven roots overwhelmed you. You fought the roots instead of the singers. Return when the weapon is the song, not the root.
The compound root-attacks bound and dissolved simultaneously. You could not escape both. Return when cutting the geas is faster than cutting the root.
The root-singers' songs drove the storm faster than you could silence them. Each dead singer made the nearest root stronger. Return when silencing is not killing.
The guardian's inverted calming song was almost complete. You could not sing the original in time. Return when healing is faster than ending.
codex: The Root Storm tests whether the deity can calm a living system that is destroying itself. The roots are not enemies — they are victims of corrupted geas. The Hollow's strategy: turn the support system against itself, so the road destroys its own foundation.

The compound root-attacks — binding and dissolving simultaneously — are the Tuatha Gate's most painful weapon: the support system attacking from two directions at once. The deity cannot fight the roots without wounding the forest. The only solution is to cut the geas, not the root.

The root-singers are the storm's engine. Each song is a corrupted geas that drives roots to violence. Silencing a singer is necessary — but killing a singer releases its geas into the nearest root. The deity must silence without killing — the Tuatha art of stopping the song without ending the singer.

The storm's eye — the original root untouched by the storm — reveals the Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: the foundation does not fight. It stands. Every root that fights has been corrupted. The original root simply exists. The calm is not the absence of violence — it is the presence of the original.

intro: The Hollow Crown of Thorns. The final trial. The Hollow has grown a crown from the corrupted roots — a geas-crown that binds whoever wears it to the void. The crown sits on the original root, poisoning it.
The geas-crown is tightening. Each thorn is a corrupted geas that embeds deeper with every movement. The deity must approach the crown without moving — or the thorns tighten and the root dies.

The crown has consumed the original root's first geas. The binding that sustained the forest — 'I bind the void to the forest' — is now 'I bind the forest to the void.' The crown speaks the inversion as law.

The final confrontation. The crown cannot be removed without killing the root — and the root cannot survive with the crown. The deity must find a third option: wear the crown and transform it, or let the root die and regrow from the corpse.
enemy: The Hollow Crown of Thorns. Each thorn is a corrupted geas that embeds deeper with movement. The more you struggle, the tighter it binds. The crown wants you to move.
The crown is spawning thorn-constructs from the original root's bark. Each one is a piece of the root that has been consumed. They attack because the root's own geas is inverted.
Hollow crown-singers. They sing the inverted geas — 'I bind the forest to the void' — in the original root's voice. The root hears its own voice serving the Hollow.
The crown itself — a living geas that has consumed the root's foundation. It cannot be removed without killing the root. It cannot stay without killing the root. The third option is the only way.
mid: The crown tightens with movement. Do not struggle. Approach without moving — through will, not through the body. The crown wants you to fight. Refuse to fight.
The thorn-constructs are pieces of the root. Do not destroy them — they are the root. Dispel the inversion, not the bark. The root's geas is corrupted, but the bark is still the root's.
The crown-singers sing in the root's voice. Do not silence them — sing the original louder. The root must hear both songs and choose. The choice is the root's — not yours.

The crown cannot be removed or left. Find the third option. Wear the crown and transform it from within — turn the binding into a healing. The thorns that bind can also graft. The geas that curses can also cure.
victory: The crown is transformed. The thorns that bound now graft. The geas that cursed now heals. The original root is saved — and the crown is part of it now. The Silver-Root Gate is damaged but not destroyed.
The thorn-constructs are restored to the root. The bark that fought now supports. The inversion is reversed — not by force, but by transformation. The root chose the original song.
The crown-singers' inversion is silenced — not by violence, but by the louder original. The root heard both songs and chose to heal. The choice was the root's. The deity's role was to sing.

The Hollow Crown of Thorns is transformed into a Healing Crown. The third option was found: the binding that kills also heals, if worn with intention. The geas is not broken — it is redirected. The Silver-Root Gate stands.
defeat: The crown tightened with every movement. You struggled. Return when stillness is more powerful than struggle.
The thorn-constructs were pieces of the root. You destroyed them. Return when the root's bark is not the enemy, even when it fights you.
The crown-singers' inversion was louder than your original. You tried to silence them. Return when the original song is louder because it is true.
The crown could not be removed or left. You saw no third option. Return when wearing the crown and transforming it from within is visible — when the binding that kills also heals.
codex: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is the Tuatha Gate's ultimate test: can the deity save a living system by transforming the weapon that destroys it? The crown cannot be removed without killing the root. It cannot stay without killing the root. The third option is transformation — wearing the crown and turning the binding into a healing.

The geas-crown's thorns embed deeper with movement. The Hollow's strategy: provoke struggle. The more the deity fights, the tighter the binding. The defense is stillness — approaching through will, not through the body. The crown wants you to fight. The root needs you to be still.

The crown-singers sing the inverted geas in the root's own voice. The root hears its own voice serving the Hollow. The defense is not silence — it is a louder original. The root must hear both songs and choose. The choice is the root's. The deity's role is to sing.

The Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: the binding that kills also heals, if worn with intention. The geas that curses can also cure. The thorns that bind can also graft. The third option is not a compromise — it is a transformation. The crown is not removed. It is worn. And the wearing changes both the crown and the wearer. The root is saved — and the crown is part of it now.

intro: The root network has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign geas-data. Every binding you swore, every cut you made, every wound you inflicted is recorded in the roots.
The corrupted roots now carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence. Each cut you made to save the forest is now a vulnerability the Hollow can exploit.
The Sídhe Mound expects your Normal campaign healing approach. Every technique you used to redirect, calm, or transform has been analyzed and countered.
The final trial of this chapter has been regrown. The Normal campaign victory is recorded — and the Elite version asks whether your healing was real or whether the root healed despite you.
enemy: Elite root-rot wraiths carrying your Normal campaign geas-data. They know which bindings you cut and which you left — and they target the ones you spared.
The corrupted roots carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence against you. Each cut is proof you harmed the forest.
The root-singers expect your Normal campaign calming approach. They have counter-songs for every technique that worked before.
The regrown trial guardian speaks with the root's voice and your Normal campaign voice. It asks: did you heal the root, or did the root heal itself?
mid: The wraiths target the roots you spared in the Normal campaign. Do not protect the same roots — the Hollow expects it. Find new roots to heal.
The wounds are evidence. Do not defend your cuts — demonstrate new healing. The root does not remember the intention. It remembers the wound.
The counter-songs are designed for your Normal campaign approach. Sing a new song — one the Hollow has not heard.
The guardian questions your healing. Do not answer with words. Answer with healing the root did not expect — healing that proves the root could not have done it alone.
victory: Chapter 1 holds — but the root network has recorded this healing too. The deeper chambers will test whether the new approach is real or simply a new pattern.
The corrupted roots are calmed — but they recorded your new healing. The Hollow studies healing across campaigns.
The counter-songs are silenced — but the root-singers heard your new song. The deeper chambers will have counter-songs for it too.
The guardian falls — but the question remains. The Elite answer: the healing was real because it was new — because the root could not have healed itself in a way it had never seen.
defeat: The wraiths targeted the roots you spared. You protected the same roots. Return when your healing is not pattern — it is creation.
The wounds were evidence against you. You defended your cuts. Return when new healing is more powerful than defending old wounds.
The counter-songs countered your Normal campaign approach. You had no new song. Return when healing is creation, not repetition.
The guardian's question held: the root healed itself. Return when your healing is undeniable — when it could not have happened without you.
codex: The Elite Chapter 1 stores geas-data across campaigns. Every Normal healing becomes an Elite vulnerability.
The Gate's learning engine spans multiple campaigns. Each descent teaches the Hollow which roots the deity heals and how — and each lesson is a future weapon.
The Elite root-singers study Normal campaign songs. The deity must create new healing for each descent — because repetition is not healing. It is habit.

Each Elite victory teaches the Hollow how to counter the next deity's healing. The root network is not just a living system — it is an archive of every wound ever inflicted and every healing ever attempted.
